full_name: Nonconvex Stochastic Block Mirror Descent (SBMD) for stochastic composite block optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020, Section 6.3 (Theorem 6.9)

problem.description: The nonconvex stochastic composite block problem studied in Section 6.3.

variable_space.math: X=X_1\times X_2\times\cdots\times X_b,\quad\text{where }X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i},\ i=1,\ldots,b,\text{ are closed convex sets with }n_1+n_2+\cdots+n_b=n.

assumptions.name: Separable_chi_6_3_4
assumptions.math: \text{Moreover, the nonsmooth component }\chi(\cdot)\text{ is still convex and separable, i.e. }\chi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^b\chi_i(x^{(i)})\quad \forall x\in X,\quad\text{where }\chi_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to\mathbb{R}\text{ are closed and convex.}

assumptions.name: Product_space_6_3_5
assumptions.math: X=X_1\times X_2\times\cdots\times X_b,\quad\text{where }X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i},\ i=1,\ldots,b,\text{ are closed convex sets with }n_1+n_2+\cdots+n_b=n.

assumptions.name: DGF_strong_convexity_section_6_3
assumptions.math: \nu_i:X_i\to\mathbb{R}\text{ be the distance generating function with modulus }1\text{ with respect to }\|\cdot\|_i,\text{ and }V_i\text{ be the associated prox-function.}

assumptions.name: Algorithm_6_1_stepsize_condition
assumptions.math: x_1\in X,\quad \{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 1}\ \text{s.t.}\ \gamma_k<2/L_i,\ i=1,\ldots,b,\quad p_i\in[0,1],\ i=1,\ldots,b,\quad \sum_{i=1}^b p_i=1.

assumptions.name: Stochastic_gradient_of_f_context_6_3_12
assumptions.math: \text{Compute the }i_k\text{-th block of the (stochastic) gradient }G_{i_k}\text{ of }f(\cdot)\text{ at }x_k\text{ satisfying }\mathbb{E}[G_{i_k}]=U_{i_k}^Tg(x_k)\text{ and }\mathbb{E}[\|G_{i_k}-U_{i_k}^Tg(x_k)\|_{i_k,*}^2]\le \bar{\sigma}_k^2.

initialization.math: x_1\in X,\quad \{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 1}\ \text{s.t.}\ \gamma_k<2/L_i,\ i=1,\ldots,b,\quad p_i\in[0,1],\ i=1,\ldots,b,\quad \sum_{i=1}^b p_i=1.

main_theorem.rate: Finite-N expected squared composite projected-gradient bound; under deterministic uniform sampling and gamma_k = 1 / max_i L_i, Corollary 6.12 gives an O(b max_i L_i / N) bound.
main_theorem.measure: expected squared composite projected-gradient norm, with expectation taken w.r.t. i_k, G_{i_k}, and R

key_lemmas.name: Proposition_6_2_composite_projected_gradient_optimality
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }x\in X\text{ be given and }P_X(x,y,\gamma)\text{ be defined as in (6.3.8) for some }\gamma>0.\text{ Also let us denote }x^+:=x-\gamma P_X(x,g(x),\gamma).\text{ Then there exists }p_i\in\partial\chi_i(U_i^Tx^+)\text{ s.t. }U_i^Tg(x^+)+p_i\in -N_{X_i}(U_i^Tx^+)+B_i((L_i\gamma+Q)\|P_X(x,g(x),\gamma)\|_i),\ i=1,\ldots,b,\text{ where }B_i(\epsilon):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}:\|v\|_{i,*}\le \epsilon\}\text{ and }N_{X_i}(U_i^Tx^+)\text{ denotes the normal cone of }X_i\text{ at }U_i^Tx^+.
key_lemmas.role: Relates small composite projected gradient to an approximate first-order optimality inclusion for the block composite problem; it motivates the stationarity measure used in Theorem 6.9.

proof.description: Record the source-local P_{X_i} notation mismatch before the proof identity. Eq. This step flags source_gap:prox_point_vs_gradient_mapping rather than deriving the identity from (6.3.6) and (6.3.8).

Record the PDF's printed block identity for U_i^T x^+. Because of the P_{X_i} notation mismatch flagged in previous_step:1, this identity is treated as a source assertion, not as a consequence of Composite_projected_gradient_6_3_8 and Prox_mapping_6_3_6 alone.
proof.produces: Source-asserted block prox identity for U_i^T x^+.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma_6_7_prox_inequalities
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }x_{k+1}\text{ be defined in (6.3.13), and denote }g_k\equiv P_X(x_k,\nabla f(x_k),\gamma_k)\text{ and }\tilde{g}_k\equiv P_{X_{i_k}}(x_k,U_{i_k}G_{i_k},\gamma_k).\text{ We have }\langle G_{i_k},\tilde{g}_k\rangle\ge \|\tilde{g}_k\|^2+\frac{1}{\gamma_k}[\chi(x_{k+1})-\chi(x_k)],\quad \|\tilde{g}_k-U_{i_k}^Tg_k\|_{i_k}\le \|G_{i_k}-U_{i_k}^T\nabla f(x_k)\|_{i_k,*}.
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the one-step prox lower bound and the stochastic-vs-exact block projected-gradient comparison used in Theorem 6.9.

proof.description: Record the source-local update/prox-point mismatch before using the sampled-block update as a prox optimality condition. Eq. The proof then treats x_{k+1}^{(i_k)} as the prox point solving (6.3.6) and later asserts gamma_k tilde{g}_k=U_{i_k}^T(x_k-x_{k+1}); this step records that source_gap rather than deriving those facts from (6.3.8) and (6.3.13) alone.
